summary: A rebuilt explore/exploit loop: ONE book, THREE force postures (armour | gunline | swarm), one choice per push, scored on a CENTRED reward. The reward is an exchange ratio — enemy units we watched die, plus structures we razed, minus our own dead — over the push's own committed cost, minus a running mean of our own recent pushes. Centring is the whole redesign: any bias common to all postures (fog we cannot see through, casualties no list kept, the era's price level, how good this opponent is) enters the baseline and cancels exactly, so two postures differ in their estimates by precisely the amount they differ in truth. The doctrine prior from abdf5ac is not replaced: it is the starting value and it is bounded by WEIGHT, never by value — score = (1−λ)·prior + λ·learned + UCB bonus, with λ = 0.75·n/(n+2), a quarter of the decision at the first pull and never more than three quarters. Credit for a push goes to whichever postures actually bought the units in it, not to whatever was chosen last. Gated at D.read ≥ 0.55, the threshold beginSiege already uses — which means the entire 89-check behaviour suite, which runs its commander at Regular, is byte-identical, not just [29]. 10 anchored edits, js/ai.js only, all anchors verified at exactly 1 by python str.count. No cross-match persistence: it is deliberately deferred and the reason is stated.
why_the_old_one_failed:
Four measured fatals, and three of them share one root.

1. DEGENERACY, the one that matters. The old reward was r = (kills + 0.8·taken − lost)/cost measured against nothing, and the update ended with `q = U.clamp(q, p − DRIFT·read, p + DRIFT·read)`. Because the numerator counted every one of our casualties at full price while counting almost nothing on the other side (see 2), r carried a large NEGATIVE offset common to every arm — the reviewer measured true arm means of −0.60/−0.75/−0.85/−1.00. Every one of those sits past the same boundary, so every q landed on it: q = −0.360 at Elite, spread 0.000, pulls 5/5/5/5. With all q tied, `if (s > bs)` returns ARMS[dim][0] for ever. Twenty waves at 4,700–15,000 credits each to arrive back at today's behaviour, while the plan's own acceptance test ("q STAYS INSIDE p ± 0.45") reported PASS. The root cause is not the clamp's size. It is that a clamp bounds a VALUE: two different values pushed against one boundary become one value. A bias-carrying reward plus a value clamp is a machine for erasing differences.

2. KILLS COUNTED UNITS ONLY. The sweep walked `seenU`, which holds units; buildings live in `seenB`. A wave that flattened three emplacements, a barracks and a power plant and died short of its aim scored exactly −1.0, identical to a wave that achieved nothing. The only structure credit in the whole reward was the single objective, at 200–1,920 credits against a wave costing 4,700–15,000. That asymmetry IS the common negative offset that saturated the clamp in (1).

3. THE `rear` AXIS ARM WAS UNREACHABLE. pickApproach charges every lane `trip * 0.55`, and a rear gate sits 2·Rg further from home — 13.6 to 15.4 points — against an AXIS_PUSH of at most 14.0·read. Rear could not win at any difficulty. Worse, learn() was fed the EXECUTED class, so rear's n never advanced while T grew, its bonus C·√(ln(1+T)/3) grew without bound, and the book latched on rear permanently: a standing 14-point penalty against the two lanes the auction actually rated best. The book became an inverted log of what the existing auction was going to do anyway. The structural error: the arm named a preference that a downstream auction was free to refuse, and the code then credited the refusal to the arm.

4. IT READ A LIVE `ref` ON AN 8-SECOND WINDOW. ai.js:1307 is `function liveTrack(r) { return G.time - r.t <= 5; }`, and noteSighting states the invariant twice: `ref` is the live entity and may only be touched while liveTrack() holds. noteContact refuses to refresh r.t for a dead entity, so r.t freezes at the last LIVE sighting — anything seen near the wave that then broke contact and died anywhere at all within 8s was booked as our kill. The design cited liveTrack as its precedent for the number, and the number was not liveTrack's.

Underneath those, two majors I have also had to design around rather than inherit: attribution ("the arm chosen at settle k−1 built wave k") was false, because groundArmy() counts the marching wave so production STOPS while a wave is alive and winning, and launchGroundWave re-forms attackWave from `army.slice(0, waveSize+6)` — the next "wave" is largely the same hulls bought under an earlier arm; and the emphasis arms could not change the army, because buildToward normalises inside a category and the two call sites fire independently, so multiplying rifle weights cannot buy one more rifleman relative to one more tank. Measured, three of four arms moved the queue by well under one unit a wave.
design:
THE SHAPE: one book, three postures, one choice a push.

  armour   the wave is hulls.  More tanks, fewer tubes, fewer bodies.
  gunline  the wave is tubes.  Howitzers, rockets and spotters; fewer hulls.
  swarm    the wave is bodies. Rifles and missile teams, and many of them.

Three, and the number is arithmetic rather than taste. Measured off the launch cadence: Veteran (waveTime 150) yields six to eight pushes in a 25-minute match, Elite (118) eight to eleven, Commander (95) eleven to fourteen. Ten arms over that horizon is one pull an arm — the commander ends the battle knowing nothing and looking random, which is the owner's complaint with extra steps. Three arms get two to six pulls each, which is enough to abandon a posture that is plainly failing. That is honestly the whole of what one match can teach, and the design says so out loud instead of promising convergence it cannot deliver.

WHAT MAKES A POSTURE REAL — the fix for the "arms do not change the army" major. A posture bites in two places, because one is not enough.

  (a) It reweights counterMix's OUTPUT, in a wrapper stanceMix() used only at the one call site that spends money. One line is the hard bound: `if (o[role] === undefined) continue;` — a posture reweights what the picture already asked for and can never put a role on the list counterMix left off. The same monoculture floor counterMix applies to its own answer is re-applied to the leaned one, so a posture may lean a queue and may not empty it. Multipliers up to 2.10, scaled by grip, because the previous attempt's 0.7-of-a-vehicle arms were unmeasurable at any horizon.

  (b) It moves the INFANTRY-TO-VEHICLE SPLIT, which nothing in this file has ever been able to move. stanceSplit() holds whichever queue is already past the posture's target infantry share (armour 0.40, gunline 0.52, swarm 0.68, each pulled toward the neutral 0.55 by grip). That is a 14-point swing between the extreme postures at Veteran and 24 at Commander — two to four units of a sixteen-unit wave, unmistakable in play and measurable in a probe. It is a PREFERENCE and never a stall: if the preferred queue buys nothing (broke, or the role has no unit this era) the held queue is released on the same think.

THE EXACT UPDATE RULE.

  Episode = one push. Opened and extended by bookWave(), which is already the one place a wave is committed — the ground launch and the landing that joins one — so an amphibious theatre is inside the loop rather than quietly outside it. Closed when the wave is empty, when the next push is committed, or after 2·waveTime as a backstop.

  Raw reward   r = clamp((kills + razed − lost) / cost, −1.2, +2.0),
               scored only if cost ≥ 1,800 (a probe is not evidence).
  Advantage    A = r − base                (base = pre-update running mean)
  Baseline     base += (r − base)/min(n_b, 6)      — tracks, never freezes
  Credit       w[a] = the cost share of the push that posture a actually bought;
               w[chosen] = max(w[chosen], cost·0.34); renormalise so Σw = 1
  Per arm      n_a += s_a ;  q_a += (s_a / min(n_a, 8)) · (A − q_a)
  Policy       score(a) = (1−λ_a)·p_a + λ_a·q_a + C·√(ln(1+T)/n_a)
               λ_a = 0.75·n_a/(n_a+2),  C = 0.12·D.read,  T = Σ n_a
               n seeded at 1, q seeded at 0, p from doctrine()

  The first settled push sets the baseline and updates nothing — one sample cannot be compared to anything, and seeding base at 0 would inject the whole common offset into the first advantage. That costs one push and is worth it.

WHY IT CANNOT DEGENERATE — the structural answer (the algebra is in degeneracy_argument). Two changes, both aimed at the same failure:
  - the reward is centred, so no common bias survives into the estimates;
  - the bound on how far experience may carry the commander is a bound on the WEIGHT the experience carries, never on its VALUE. λ multiplies the gap between two estimates; it cannot close one. There is no clamp on q anywhere in the design.

CREDIT ASSIGNMENT — the fix for the attribution major. Each unit carries `u._arm`, stamped where the army is read (`if (!u._arm) u._arm = armNow`), which is "the posture in force when it joined the army" — one production cycle after the order, the closest honest answer available without a new field in entities.js. At settle, each posture takes the cost share of the push it actually bought. This makes the force-settle problem vanish structurally rather than by timing: it no longer matters when the choice was made, because the credit is read off what the wave was MADE OF. And it fixes the perverse coupling the reviewers found — while a wave is alive and winning nothing is queued, so the next push is largely the same hulls; those hulls carry the tags of the posture that bought them and that posture keeps earning or losing on them. The chosen posture keeps at least a third of the credit whatever the factory managed to deliver, which is also what keeps its pull count moving so it cannot sit unvisited with a growing bonus.

LOSSES ARE SUMMED WHERE THE CASUALTY PASSES, NOT FROM graves. reapWave() is the file's own statement that "every casualty passes here exactly once". `ep.lost += P.factionCost(u.def)` goes there. graves are capped at 60 entries and pruned by age inside graveWeight — so the pushes with the most to teach are exactly the ones whose losses a grave sweep drops, biasing the reward upward on the worst waves. Accumulating at the point of death removes that bias entirely and removes an edit.

KILLS AND RAZINGS — see fog_argument for the observation proof. Kills are swept on the picture's own 0.8s clock (not think()'s 0.9–3.6s) because liveTrack is five seconds. Razings are credited at the one line in forgetStale where a structure is struck off, which is the only place the commander ever learns a structure is gone, and it learns it by going back and looking. Structures are priced at worthOf() — the same valuation objectives() picks targets with, so the learner and the target picker agree about what a barracks is worth, and a defence is 40% of its cost there, which is what stops a wave farming sandbags for reward. The kill radius is the wave's own deepest ground weapon plus four tiles rather than a constant, because a flat radius under-credits precisely the posture that fights at twenty tiles: one arm measured on a shorter ruler than the others is a rigged comparison.

HOW IT COMPOSES WITH THE DOCTRINE PRIOR. p_a comes from doctrine(P.faction, P.era) and nothing else — no phantom module, no new table. A posture's prior is the mean of the doctrine entries that posture spends on, centred across the three so it is a preference and not a level:
  raw.armour  = (dm.heavy.mbt + dm.heavy.heavy)/2
  raw.swarm   = (dm.heavy.at + dm.infantry.mg + dm.infantry.rifle)/3
  raw.gunline = 1
  p_a = clamp((raw_a − mean(raw))·0.6, ±0.30)
DOCT_SET deliberately carries no entry for spg, mlrs, sniper or radarv — its own comment says the prior has no opinion about them — so gunline opens at the flat share and must earn its place from evidence. That is the honest reading of a table that says nothing, and it is better than inventing an entry.
  WEIGHT EARLY vs LATE: λ = 0.75·n/(n+2). At the first pull the manual carries 75% of the decision; at two pulls 62.5%/37.5%; at four pulls 50/50; at eight 60% learned; in the limit the manual still carries 25% and never less. Concretely: the widest edge doctrine() can express (0.55 against 1.80) arrives as a prior gap of 0.30; at λ=0.75 an observed advantage gap of 0.10 in exchange ratio overturns it, and at λ=0.25 it does not. That is "don't let AI use the pre-trained knowledge entirely… with some flexibility in a reasonable way" written as two numbers.
  An era step re-equips the army — our own MBT goes 690 → 1,500 credits and its gun with it — so bookEraWatch() re-reads the manual and halves q and n. Not a reset: half of what was learned is about this opponent and this ground, and neither changed. This also answers the review finding that the old prior was cached against an empty picture and never followed the generation.

DIFFICULTY. learnOn() is D.read ≥ 0.55 — the same threshold beginSiege already uses to decide a commander reads ground well enough to stand off and shell it, so it is an existing idiom and not a new constant. Recruit (0) and Regular (0.35) never open an episode, never choose a posture, never lean a queue: armNow stays null, stanceMix hands back counterMix's object untouched, stanceSplit returns −1, and the two buildToward calls run in the same order with the same arguments. Above the gate every lever is scaled by grip = D.read. The gate and the horizon agree: the tiers that get the loop (Veteran 6–8 pushes, Elite 8–11, Commander 11–14, Warlord 14–18) are exactly the tiers with enough pushes for three arms.

WHEN THERE IS NO CHOICE, THE LOOP STAYS OUT OF THE WAY. armReady() tests the roles a posture actually spends on, through unitFor against our own roster — not a proxy (the old armReady tested spg and mbt, which every faction owns in every era, so it reduced to `P.tech >= 2` and prevented nothing). If fewer than two postures are fieldable — before the factory, or on a roster that genuinely lacks a system — armNow is null and the commander plays plain doctrine. That respects the owner's realism rule: a faction may simply not have a posture available, and the answer is to strike it off, not to invent one.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE, and why:
  - No axis book. The old `rear` arm was unreachable because pickApproach's own trip cost outweighs any bias the arm could apply, and because the arm named a preference an auction was free to refuse. A posture cannot be refused — it is applied directly to purchase weights and the queue gate — which is the structural reason fatal 3 cannot recur here. Steering lanes needs pickApproach's cost function changed, not a bandit bolted to it.
  - No tempo book. `mass` in the old design multiplied only the launch gate, not the build target, so it did not build a bigger wave: it waited for production overshoot and stalled. Fixing it means scaling wantSize, which is a separate change that should be measured on its own.
  - No air or naval arm. Aircraft are not in attackWave, reapWave never sees one die, and a sortie flies against warAim on its own clock. An air arm would put noise into the book in exchange for a column nothing could score.
  - No cross-match persistence in v1. It is the only thing that would push n past three or four, and I want it — but persisting a two-sample estimate persists noise, and it makes the opening of every match with that faction more fixed, which is the owner's original complaint. It is a second pass, conditional on measurement 4 below coming back positive.

COST. One extra O(seenU) pass every 0.8s while a push is open, alongside the one forgetStale already does, with a first test of `r.scored || !r.ref || !r.ref.dead` that rejects almost everything. One O(army) stamp loop per think, over a list already being walked. Three arms scored per settle. No new G.rng() call anywhere, so seeded replays stay deterministic — variety comes from outcomes, not from dice, which is the point.
degeneracy_argument:
THE CLAIM: two postures with different true values end up with different estimates, and the gap between the estimates equals the gap between the truths.

Setup. Let push k be built under posture a_k and settle with raw exchange ratio r_k. Decompose

    r_k = μ(a_k) + c + ε_k

where μ(a) is the posture's own contribution, ε_k is zero-mean noise, and c is EVERYTHING true of the battle rather than of the choice: the kills the fog hid, the casualties no list kept, the price level of this era (4,721 credits a wave for a 1950s KPA against 15,039 for a 2020s ROC), how good this opponent is, how defended this map is, how far the objective is. c is the term that killed the previous design.

Step 1 — the baseline absorbs c. `base` is a running mean of r with step 1/min(n_b, 6), so in steady state

    base → E[r] = c + Σ_a f_a μ(a) = c + μ̄

where f_a is the pull frequency.

Step 2 — the advantage deletes c exactly.

    A_k = r_k − base = (μ(a_k) + c + ε_k) − (c + μ̄) = (μ(a_k) − μ̄) + ε_k

c has cancelled, for any size of c. That single line is what the old design lacked. Note this is a subtraction, not a clamp: it does not compress anything, it shifts everything by the same amount.

Step 3 — the estimate converges to the advantage. q_a is a weighted running mean of the A's credited to a (step s/min(n_a, 8)), so E[q_a] → μ(a) − μ̄, and for any two postures

    E[q_1] − E[q_2] = (μ(1) − μ̄) − (μ(2) − μ̄) = μ(1) − μ(2)

The difference in estimates IS the difference in true values. Exactly, with no scaling constant and no residual bias.

Step 4 — nothing downstream can close the gap. The score is

    score(a) = (1 − λ_a)·p_a + λ_a·q_a + C·√(ln(1+T)/n_a),   λ_a = 0.75·n_a/(n_a+2)

so score(1) − score(2) = (1−λ)(p_1 − p_2) + λ(q_1 − q_2) + (bonus difference). λ is a WEIGHT: it multiplies the gap. It is zero only at n_a = 0, which cannot occur because every arm is seeded at n = 1 and every settle adds strictly positive count to the chosen arm. There is no clamp on q anywhere in the design — the old `U.clamp(q, p − DRIFT·read, p + DRIFT·read)` is gone and is not replaced by anything that acts on a value.

WORKED ON THE REVIEWER'S OWN MEASURED NUMBERS. The reviewer ran the old block with true arm means −0.60 / −0.75 / −0.85 / −1.00 and got, at Elite (read 0.80, 20 waves), every arm at exactly q = −0.360 = p − 0.45·0.80, spread 0.000, pulls 5/5/5/5. Take the same four means here, with a plausible committed pull frequency f = (0.5, 0.2, 0.2, 0.1):

    μ̄  = 0.5(−0.60) + 0.2(−0.75) + 0.2(−0.85) + 0.1(−1.00) = −0.72
    q  = +0.12, −0.03, −0.13, −0.28      spread 0.40

The spread of the estimates is 0.40, which is exactly the spread of the true means. The common −0.72 that pinned every old arm to the same boundary is simply not in the estimates. A design that hits the boundary is impossible: the advantages are centred by construction, so they straddle zero — a weighted mean of them is zero — and no boundary lies on both sides of zero at once.

DOES IT ACTUALLY EXPLOIT? The other half of "randomness wearing a bandit's clothes" is a bonus that never lets the leader keep the lead. Take the numbers above at T = 12 with pulls 6/2/2/2 and C = 0.12·0.80 = 0.096:

    value gap, best vs worst, at λ(n=6) = 0.5625 and λ(n=2) = 0.375:
        0.5625(0.12) − 0.375(−0.28) = 0.067 + 0.105 = 0.172
    bonus gap:  0.096(√(2.565/2) − √(2.565/6)) = 0.096(1.132 − 0.654) = 0.046

0.172 > 0.046: the leader is not unseated by exploration. It commits. Generally: for the arm being pulled n_a grows with T, so its bonus falls like √(ln T / T) → 0; for an arm left alone n_a is fixed and its bonus creeps up like √(ln T) — 1.18 at T=3, 1.52 at T=10, 1.75 at T=20 — which guarantees nothing is unreachable but is far too slow to unseat a posture that is paying. That is "the exploration bonus shrinks with visits" with no schedule to tune.

WORKED OPENING, to show it neither dithers nor sticks. Priors p = (+0.10, 0, −0.10), all n = 1, grip 0.8. Bonuses equal, so the opening choice is argmax of the prior: armour. Two bad pushes (A = −0.40 each):
    after 1: q_armour = −0.20, λ = 0.375 → score = 0.625(0.10) + 0.375(−0.20) + 0.096√(ln5/2) = 0.0625 − 0.075 + 0.086 = 0.074
             gunline (untouched) = 0.75(0) + 0.096√(ln5/1) = 0.122   → gunline is tried at push 3
    after 2 under armour instead: q = −0.267, λ = 0.45 → 0.055 − 0.120 + 0.0745 = 0.0095 vs gunline 0.128.
The incumbent is abandoned when it stops paying, not on a timer and not on a coin.

WHERE THE CLAIM STOPS, said plainly rather than hidden. Everything above is about expectations. With n_a = 2 or 3 the estimator's standard error is roughly σ/√n; taking the reviewer's own per-wave reward noise of σ ≈ 0.35 that is ±0.20 to ±0.25, comparable to the gaps being resolved. λ is exactly the defence: at n = 2 it is 0.375, so a noisy estimate can move the score by at most 0.375 × its error. So the design claims: the estimates are unbiased and separate in expectation, and within one Veteran match the commander will usually only have enough evidence to abandon a posture that is clearly failing, not to rank the two survivors. At Commander and Warlord (11–18 pushes, 4–6 pulls an arm) it will rank them. If measurement 3 below shows the learner cannot beat a shuffled-reward control at Elite, the honest conclusion is that the horizon is too short and the loop should be cut to two arms — not that the constants need tuning.
fog_argument:
"ai should have the same fog like us. don't assume and make ai know everything." Every input to the reward, the credit assignment and the policy, named, with how it is observed.

1. cost (the denominator) — Σ P.factionCost(u.def) over the push's own members, computed in learnCommit from attackWave. Our units, at what we paid. Nothing to fog.

2. lost — accumulated in reapWave(), which walks attackWave only, at the moment one of OUR units is found dead. Our own casualties, priced at our own cost. Nothing to fog. (It is summed there rather than from `graves` because graves cap at 60 entries and prune by age — so the pushes that went worst would under-report their own losses. That is a correctness fix, not a fog question.)

3. kills — a walk over `seenU`, which is written ONLY by noteContact → noteSighting: hostile only (noteContact rejects `e.owner === P || G.allied(P, e.owner)`), sub only if G.canSeeSub, low-observable only from closer in, structure only if buildProgress ≥ 1. Four gates before a credit:
   (a) `r.t >= ep.t` — we were still holding the track after this push was committed. A contact lost before the push began cannot be billed to it.
   (b) `liveTrack(r)` — ai.js:1307, `G.time - r.t <= 5`. This is the file's OWN invariant, stated twice in noteSighting and enforced by trackedEntity: `ref` is the live entity and may only be touched while liveTrack() holds. I touch `r.ref.dead` inside that window and nowhere else. The previous design used eight seconds and cited liveTrack as its precedent, which was untrue of the code it cited; that is fatal 4 and it is gone.
   (c) `staleness((r.x/CFG.TILE)|0, (r.y/CFG.TILE)|0, now) <= 6` — something of ours overlooked the tile it was last seen on within six seconds, read off our own `look` grid (painted by intelSweep from our own units' sightR, at 4-second resolution). Six is the same threshold forgetStale uses to decide we have been back and looked. This is the look-grid check the reviewers said was "right there and unused".
   (d) it fell within the push's own reach of the push's own centroid, both of which are properties of our own units.
   The sweep runs inside intelSweep's 0.8s cadence, not think()'s 0.9–3.6s, precisely so that a kill is noticed while the track that saw it is still live rather than reconstructed afterwards from a stale memory.

4. the price of a kill — a new `cost` field on the seenU record, written AT CONTACT beside role / armor / plate / cat, from `e.def.cost`. This is the published catalogue price of a vehicle we have recognised by sight — the same class of fact as `plate`, and the file already argues that case in noteSighting's own comment ("what class of thing it is and how thick its glacis is are what a recognition manual gives you the instant you have it in view"). It is not read off the enemy's books, it is not their paid cost (their costMul is not consulted), and it is recorded at the moment of contact so that nothing is ever read off a stale `ref`.

5. razed — credited at exactly one line, inside forgetStale, at the transition where a structure is struck off the plot. forgetStale sets `gone` only under `staleness(r.tx, r.ty, now) < 6 && r.t < now - 6`: we went back, looked at where it stood, and it was not there. That IS the observation; there is nothing to add to it. `ref.dead` is NOT consulted for structures — the previous design did, and that converted a building destroyed in fog by somebody else into reward. Value is worthOf(r.key), our own hand-authored valuation of a structure we identified by sight, and the same one objectives() picks targets with. Gated on proximity to our own push.

6. the credit shares — `u._arm` on our own units and P.factionCost on our own defs. Ours.

7. the prior — doctrine(P.faction, P.era), built from CFG.DMG, the penetration model, WEAPONS, UNITS and unitFor over OUR OWN roster and a mean over the eight published rosters of the period. It is a training manual computed from published tables: it says what to build given what was seen, and never says what is there. It takes no picture argument and reads no sighting.

8. feasibility — unitFor(P.faction, role, P.era) and P.tech. Our own roster and our own tech level.

9. the baseline and the book — our own past rewards, and therefore recursively fog-clean.

10. the posture's effect — stanceMix leans counterMix(foeArms()), and foeArms is already the fogged reading counterMix has always used (seenU aged at D.memory). The lean touches only roles counterMix already put on the list, so the posture cannot see further than counterMix does.

NOT READ ANYWHERE IN THIS CHANGE: any enemy player's units[] or buildings[] array, their cash, their tech, their queues, their faction, their production, their era, any entity we have not sighted, any `ref` outside the five-second window, `ref.dead` on a structure, or anything about who is winning apart from our own credit exchange.

THE ONE RESIDUAL LIMIT, stated rather than papered over: proximity is not causation. Something killed beside our push by an ally, or by the human, is credited to us, and something killed beside the human's army by us is credited to them. The commander cannot see who fired the last shot. That is a bound, it is identical for all three postures so it cannot bias the ranking between them, and it is the same bound a human watching that same fight is under. Measurement 5 below is the probe that pins the size of it.

State lives in the closure with the rest of the picture for the same reason everything else does: two commanders sharing one book would be sharing one battle's worth of experience. edits.why: The fix for fatal 2 - kills counted units only, so razing an enemy base scored zero. This line is the exact moment the commander learns a structure is not there any more, and it learns it the only honest way: by going back and looking (forgetStale requires staleness < 6). It is therefore the only place a razing may be credited, and `ref.dead` - which the previous design used and which sees through fog - is never consulted.

The kill sweep and the settle check must run on the picture's 0.8s clock, not think()'s 0.9-3.6s, because liveTrack() is five seconds: a kill has to be noticed while the track that saw it is still live. Placed immediately after forgetStale so a structure struck off on this tick is credited to the push that took it.

bookWave() is already the one place a wave is COMMITTED - the ground launch and the landing that joins one - so it is the one place the episode is opened and extended. Hooking here rather than at launchGroundWave is what puts amphibious theatres inside the loop instead of leaving them silently outside it with the postures still leaning every purchase, which is a hole the previous design had.

Our own losses, summed where the casualty passes rather than off `graves`. This function's own comment states that every casualty passes here exactly once. graves cap at 60 entries and graveWeight prunes by age during the wave, so a grave sweep under-counts losses on precisely the pushes that went worst - biasing the reward upward in the direction that most corrupts a ranking. Accumulating here removes that bias entirely.

The previous push must be closed before the next is committed or the two share one casualty list and one set of kills. Placed inside the launch branch, not before it, so it fires only when a push actually begins. Settling is also what chooses the posture the next few minutes of production are bought under.

The three places the posture actually spends money: the purchase tag that makes credit assignment honest, the leaned mixture, and the split gate that is the only thing in this file able to move the infantry-to-vehicle ratio. With no posture in force (Recruit, Regular, or fewer than two postures fieldable) `hold` is -1, stanceMix returns counterMix's object untouched, and the two buildToward calls run in the same order with the same arguments as today - the release block below them cannot fire, because neither of its branches matches hold === -1.

measurements_requested: 1. THE SUITE, AND THE STRONGER CLAIM. Run _behtest.html headless and confirm 89 passed / 0 failed. Then confirm the stronger property this design buys: the FULL log must be byte-identical to the current build, not merely the same pass count. _behtest.html:37 defaults opt-diff to "regular" and the harness at lines 333-337 sets opt-map/era/aera/cash/seed/fog/3d and never opt-diff, so every commander in all 89 checks runs at read 0.35, below the 0.55 gate: learnOn() is false, armNow is null, stanceMix returns counterMix's object untouched, stanceSplit returns -1, the split-release block cannot fire, and no episode is ever opened. If ANY line of that log has moved, the gate is wrong and the change must not land. Inside [29], the four printed figures (tank destroyer and MG before and after the infantry flood) must be unchanged: intel().mix still calls the unedited counterMix.

2. DOES IT MOVE THE ARMY - the question that killed the previous attempt. Copy _comp.html, print AI.intelOf(E).learn on every change of .waves plus the composition split, and run Elite vs Elite for 25 minutes. Two numbers: (a) the infantry share of groundArmy() under `swarm` must exceed the share under `armour` by at least 10 percentage points sustained over a wave interval (predicted 14 at Veteran, 19 at Elite, 24 at Commander) - if it is under 5 the split gate is not biting and the arms are unlearnable, exactly as the previous design's were; (b) the spg+mlrs share of the vehicle queue under `gunline` must be at least 1.6x its share under `armour`. Report both per difficulty tier.

3. THE ACCEPTANCE GATE: A SHUFFLED-REWARD CONTROL. A reviewer of the previous attempt showed that 'pull counts uneven' and 'spread > 0.15' both fire on pure noise about half the time at this horizon, so neither is evidence on its own. Build a control where learnSettle() credits the advantage to a uniformly random posture instead of to the push's own membership, everything else identical. Run 6 paired seeds Elite vs Elite, 25 minutes, learner against control. The learner is real only if BOTH hold: max(q)-min(q) at the final whistle is larger in the learner than in the control on at least 5 of 6 seeds, AND the learner's mean reward over the last third of the match exceeds the control's. If it does not, the honest conclusion is that the horizon is too short for three arms - cut to two (armour, swarm) rather than tuning constants.

4. IS IT BETTER, NOT JUST DIFFERENT. 6 matches with EXPLORE = 0 and the posture pinned to argmax of the prior (pure doctrine, no learning) against 6 with the loop on, same seeds, at Elite and at Commander. The loop must beat the pinned-doctrine arm's mean reward over the last third by at least 0.08 r/push, and must not LOSE to it at any tier. Report the mean r per push for both arms and both tiers. Exploration is not free - the reviewer measured it costing about 0.013 r/push where the prior is already correct - so a flat or negative result at Elite means EXPLORE should drop to 0.06, and a negative result at Commander means the loop should not ship.

5. FOG HONESTY, ASSERTED RATHER THAN ARGUED. Log every credited kill with (G.time - r.t), the staleness of the tile it was last seen on, and its distance from the push centroid in tiles. Assert on 100% of credited kills: age <= 5, staleness <= 6, distance <= ep.r. Assert no credit is ever taken with ep null. Then the bound I cannot close: on a 3+ player map, count what share of credited kills were killed by somebody other than this commander. If that share exceeds about 15%, proximity is doing too much work and the radius should come down.

6. THE SPLIT GATE MUST NOT STALL. Time-to-wantSize from match start at Elite must be within 10% of the current build. Separately, count how often the release branch fires (the preferred queue bought nothing and the held one was let through); if it fires on more than about a third of thinks the deadband is too narrow.

7. THE HORIZON, MEASURED RATHER THAN ESTIMATED. Count SETTLED pushes per 25-minute match at veteran / elite / commander / warlord, and for the turtle and rusher personalities (waveTime 999 and 55 - a factor of eighteen in sample budget). If Veteran yields under 5 settled pushes, raise LEARN_READ from 0.55 to 0.80 so the loop only runs where it can learn. If turtle yields 1, confirm the intended behaviour: it plays pure doctrine, which is correct and not a bug.

8. THE REWARD'S OWN COMPONENTS. Print kills / razed / lost / cost for every settled push. Three checks: razed must be non-zero on at least one push per match (if it is always zero the forgetStale hook is not firing and fatal 2 is still live); the mean advantage A across all settled pushes must sit near zero, which is the direct test that the centring is working; and Sum(n) across the book must grow by exactly 1.0 per scored push.
